SMTO-LLM-0031 — SMTO couldn't use the model's answer

GUID: 1a0ac7e2-d3d0-48a5-b22f-8c1447547da3
Slug: llm-response-error
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • The model replied, but not in a form SMTO could use. This message comes from an older or outside record, so it doesn't say which part was wrong.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and select Check saved model. It tests whether the current model can answer in the form SMTO needs, which this old record can't tell you.
  2. If the check passes, try the work again in a new task. Current SMTO reports a more specific message that names what was wrong with the answer.
  3. If a different error appears, follow the steps in that error's panel instead of these. That newer message points to the actual cause, such as a blank or broken answer.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model reports passed, and the new task completes its model steps.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with any newer error, to the person who manages SMTO or your model service. Don't keep sending the same request unchanged; fix what the newer error names first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A model result was recorded under the legacy llm_response_error category, which the resolver keeps only for old or external records; no current code raises it, and it does not identify whether syntax, structure or transport failed.

What this means

  • This retained compatibility category identifies an unusable model result without a more specific live producer condition; exact syntax, schema and transport failures have separate identities. No current direct producer was found for llm_response_error; the resolver retains the alias for old or external payloads. It supplies no execution certainty.

Why this can happen

  • This retained compatibility category identifies an unusable model result without a more specific live producer condition; exact syntax, schema and transport failures have separate identities.

How to diagnose it

  • Use the saved stage and any more specific typed cause; if neither was retained, preserve the occurrence rather than reconstructing a cause from prose.

How to fix it

  • Treat this as a historical record: inspect any saved provider diagnostics and raw response preview, and confirm the model's tool-calling and structured-output support with Check saved model. Reproduce in a new task; current code reports a specific error (invalid JSON, schema validation, empty response or a transport category) that names the real cause.
  • Inspect provider diagnostics and supported structured response format.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A new controlled response passes the caller's actual response contract; the historical occurrence remains limited to its retained evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • No current direct producer was found for llm_response_error; the resolver retains the alias for old or external payloads. It supplies no execution certainty.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
